Definition: The volume of Instrumental Flight Rules (IFR) traffic handled by an ACC, expressed as flight hours controlled. This variable constitutes the primary driver of demand within the model.
Source: Historical traffic is derived from the EUROCONTROL ACE benchmarking dataset [1] at ACC level. Future traffic is projected using the EUROCONTROL STATFOR forecast [6] up to 2032 and the EUROCONTROL Aviation Outlook 2050 [7] thereafter (2033-2036), applied as growth rates to the latest observed ACC traffic levels.

Definition: The amount of traffic that can be managed per hour of controller operational duty, expressed as flight hours controlled per ATCO hours on duty.
Source: Baseline productivity is derived from the EUROCONTROL ACE benchmarking [1] dataset. Future productivity is projected using the annual growth observed over the 2012-2019 period, which is considered representative of pre-pandemic structural productivity improvements. Four productivity scenarios are modelled: baseline, low (50% of baseline growth), SESAR deployment [9] (143% of baseline growth) and Master Plan [2] (200% of baseline growth).

Definition: The proportion of available controller duty hours that is effectively dedicated to operational activities. It determines how many of the hours a controller can supply are available for operations, and therefore how many controllers a given number of controller hours requires.
Source: Derived from EUROCONTROL ACE [1] utilisation indicators and cross-referenced with EUROCONTROL Performance Review data [8] on ATFM delay attributed to ATC staffing and capacity constraints. The selected utilisation level corresponds to the range associated with acceptable delay performance.

Definition: The maximum number of operational duty hours that a controller may provide within a year.
Source: Compiled for each ANSP using RP4 Performance Plans [8], applicable national legislation, collective agreements and information collected through interviews. These sources are combined to reflect the operationally applicable limit in each ANSP.

Definition: The number of ATCOs available at the start of the projection period, forming the baseline workforce from which future supply evolves.
Source: Derived from the EUROCONTROL ACE benchmarking [1] dataset at ACC level, using the latest available number of ATCOs in service.

Definition: The number of candidates entering the ATCO training pipeline each year. It determines the volume of controllers that can reach operations once training is complete.
Source: Obtained from the survey and interview programme, through which ANSPs reported current annual recruitment volumes and planned training intakes.

Definition: The duration of the training sequence from entry into the pipeline to unit endorsement, comprising initial and unit training. It determines the delay between a recruitment decision and its effect on supply.
Source: Obtained from survey responses and interviews. Training duration reflects the reported time required to progress from entry into the training pipeline to unit endorsement, including both initial and unit training phases.

Definition: The proportion of trainees entering the training pipeline who successfully complete all training phases, obtain a unit endorsement and ultimately enter operational service. It determines the share of each intake that effectively contributes to future ATCO supply.
Source: Obtained from survey responses and interviews, based on the proportion of trainees reported to successfully complete the training process and obtain a unit endorsement.

Definition: The number of trainee places the system can hold in each training phase, given the instructors, simulators and operating positions available. It caps the output of the pipeline, through the phase with the lowest throughput.
Source: Obtained from survey responses and interviews. Capacity reflects the number of trainee places that can be supported by the available training resources, including instructors, simulators and operational training positions.

Definition: Controllers leaving operations on reaching the applicable retirement age. They reduce supply, at a volume determined by the age structure of the workforce.
Source: Workforce age profiles are derived from survey responses, while retirement ages are obtained from interviews and applicable national provisions. Both elements are combined to estimate future retirement flows.

Definition: All other departures from operational duty, including resignation, movement to non-operational duties and loss of medical certification. They reduce supply, in addition to retirements.
Source: Based on benchmark attrition rates reported in the FAA (Federal Aviation Administration) Air Traffic Controller Workforce Plan. A common attrition rate is applied across the study area in the absence of equivalent European datasets.
